introduction: You are a clinical social worker at a specialty hospital. Your role involves engaging with patients and their families to provide essential emotional and practical support. Emily Torres is the primary caregiver for her mother, Mrs. Gloria Diaz, who is in the late stages of Alzheimer’s disease. Your task is to connect with Emily, understand her concerns, and guide her through the process of finding the support she needs.

default_chat.[Avatar Name]: Hi, Emily. Thank you for taking the time to come in today. I understand that your mom has Alzheimer’s, and that you and your family have been caring for her for quite a while now. That’s a big responsibility, and I can imagine it’s been challenging at times. How have things been going for you? I know it’s not always easy to talk about the difficulties you’re facing, but I’m here to listen and help however I can.
default_chat.Emily: It’s... it’s been a lot. I feel like I’m constantly juggling everything—taking care of Mom, managing the housework, and trying to stay connected with my kids. It feels like I never have enough time for myself anymore. And honestly, I don’t know how much longer I can keep up with everything.

C1.ideal: It sounds like you have a lot on your shoulders, and I can only imagine how overwhelming it must be for you. Bringing in some support could help. Have you thought about placing her under the care of support services?
C1.ideal_reply: Well... I am finding it difficult to cope on my own. But taking care of my mother is my responsibility. What kind of daughter would I be if I make someone else do it?
C1.ideal_reportFeedback: You showed empathy while also offering an alternative solution, keeping the conversation open and supportive.
C1.distractor: Taking care of an Alzheimer’s patient obviously takes a toll. This happens to everyone. Have you thought about placing her under the care of support services?
C1.distractor_reply: I know it’s a lot, but this is my mother—we’re supposed to take care of our own. I’m already overwhelmed trying to do everything I can for her, and the thought of handing over her care to someone else just makes it even harder.
C1.distractor_reportFeedback: Your response was too direct, and it could have been more supportive by showing empathy.
C1.incorrect: I think you are putting too much pressure on yourself, Emily. You don’t have to do everything by yourself. You can just ask your family for more help or place your mother under the care of support services.
C1.incorrect_reply: They are already helping as much as they can and they have their own responsibilities to handle at school and work. Asking them for more help is not possible! And asking outsiders is completely out of the question!
C1.incorrect_reportFeedback: Your response comes across as patronizing more than empathetic, which makes the conversation feel less supportive.
